knownGap.why: ours is 126.7° against ORC's 100.0° (the builder's own ISO figures are 107° loaded and 122° light): the synthetic hull has a flat, closed deck at the sheer and no open cockpit, and the mass roll-up puts the lightship's G at mid-depth; RM at 1° is 16% over in the same condition

orc.what: ORC's measured displacement 811 kg plus a crew of 4 × 80 kg (320 kg, estimated; the certificate gives 255–340 kg and says '4 crew')

polar.note: ORC rates downwind with the asymmetric spinnaker (45.64 m²); the VPP has none, so only the beat and 52–90° are compared.

pinned.why: she points 7° higher than ORC at 12 and 16 kn and her beat VMG is 4–11% over, as the J/24's is: the VPP has no heel-induced hull side force and generic sail coefficients. Reaching speeds are within 7%.

mastAftOfStem.how: ORC's measured SFJ 0.160 plus J 2.341 (ORC's own J is 2.340)

keelLeAftOfStem.how: read off the class rules' inboard profile, scaled on ORC's LOA

balance.why: Mast and forestay are measured (ORC); the keel's position and root chord are read off a class-rules drawing whose scale checks to 0.01–0.03 m. The keel's planform below the hull and the bulb are not sourced: a lifting keel is taken as constant-chord and unswept, the bulb by rule.

published.estimatedWhy: BWL is solved from ORC's sink; Tc is read off the class-rules drawing with the waterline placed by ORC's freeboards (±0.03 m). The keel's leading edge and root chord are read off the same drawing; its tip chord (taken equal: a keel that lifts through a trunk), sweep (0), section and bulb (a spheroid 4.5 diameters long holding the 286 kg) are not in any source. The rudder's draft is the builder's; its chord and position are read off the drawing.
